title: Embeddings + Rerank staged deployment PRD and fallback runbook
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: PRD to deliver a coordinated hosted API launch for the embeddings and rerank surfaces with staged deployment, explicit behavioral profiles per lane, and robust fallback policies. This ticket captures scope, acceptance criteria, rollout steps, monitoring, and rollback/runbook items needed for go/no-go decisions.
background: Customers increasingly combine similarity search with in-request reranking to improve relevance. Current hosted embeddings and rerank implementations are experimental and differ in latency/cost profiles. This initiative standardizes behavior across lanes (low-latency search, high-recall retrieval, rerank-as-a-service), defines quality gates, and introduces automated fallbacks to keep production traffic healthy during model/infra regressions.
goals: Ship stable, documented embeddings + rerank endpoints in hosted API with per-lane behavioral guarantees
Enable staged canary rollout with automated rollback triggers tied to quality and latency SLAs
Provide a fallback model pathway that preserves uptime and reasonable quality when primary models or dedicated capacity degrade
non_goals: Replacing third-party index stores (e.g., customers' FAISS/Weaviate) — integration guidance only
Major model research or new model training (we will use vetted open-source variants/pinned versions)
requirements: API surface: single /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank endpoints consistent with existing hosted inference patterns
Behavioral profiles: define at least three lane profiles: FAST_SIMILARITY, BALANCED_RECALL, HIGH_QUALITY_RERANK
Contract: per-request timeout semantics, streaming where applicable, and structured JSON contract for scores and metadata
Performance: p95 latency for FAST_SIMILARITY <= 80ms (in-region), BALANCED_RECALL p95 <= 200ms
Quality: similarity vectors must maintain cosine-similarity correlation >= 0.92 vs baseline model on established eval set
Rerank quality: pairwise NDCG@10 delta vs baseline must be >= -0.015 (regression budget), recall@50 for BALANCED_RECALL within -2% absolute
Cost: recommended default quantization/instance profile documented with expected tokens/second throughput and cost estimate
Observability: dashboards for latency, error rates, quality regressions (per-prompt-set evals), model version distribution, and fallback events
Operational: automated canary policy with thresholds, automated fallback routing policy to a lower-tier model or degraded lane, and alerting to SRE/SEV owners
Docs: PRD, SDK examples, migration notes, and conformance tests published before launch
scope_changes: 2026-02-25: Narrowed initial launch to two lanes (FAST_SIMILARITY, BALANCED_RECALL) — HIGH_QUALITY_RERANK deferred to Post-Launch cycle to reduce infra scope
2026-03-02: Added automated fallback routing requirement after SRE review; originally planned manual intervention only
2026-03-08: Replaced streaming rerank MVP with synchronous batched responses for v1 to simplify runtime integration
acceptance_criteria: Functional: /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank endpoints respond with documented schema for all lanes
Performance: Measured p95 latency and p99 latency meet lane targets in staging under representative traffic profiles
Quality: Eval harness demonstrates similarity correlation >= 0.92 and rerank NDCG within regression budget on canonical prompt sets
Operational: Canary rollout automation is deployed and verified (simulated rollback triggers applied in staging), and runbook steps verified via drill
Fallback: Fallback routing successfully shifts 100% of canary traffic to fallback model when threshold breached and recovers traffic after validation
Observability: Dashboards and alerts are live, with SLO burn rates visible and an on-call notification path configured
Documentation: SDK snippets, API reference, and migration guide reviewed by DX and published to docs.redwood.ai
Security & Compliance: KMS integration for customer-managed keys validated for Private/Enterprise lanes and security review signed-off
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): unit/integration tests, CI conformance, internal performance runs
Stage 1 (staging canary): 1% synthetic traffic + smoke traffic from internal customers for 48 hours
Stage 2 (customer canary): 5% of external traffic routed by customer cohorts with close monitoring for 72 hours
Stage 3 (regional expansion): expand to 50% in region with automated gating every 24 hours
Stage 4 (global launch): 100% rollout after 7 days of stable metrics or manual exec approval
monitoring_and_success_metrics: Latency: p50/p95/p99 per lane (regional), median and tail latency trends
Errors: 4xx/5xx and model-internal failures per 1k requests
Quality: daily evals against canonical prompt sets (similarity correlation, NDCG, recall@k) with trend alerts
Fallback rate: percent of requests routed to fallback; target < 0.5% during healthy operation
SLO burn: token cost per 1000 requests normalized; availability >= 99.8% for Hosted API tier
Customer tickets: zero P0 tickets related to correctness or major regressions in first 14 days
rollout_checklist: Design sign-off on API contract and request/response schema
Model onboarding: baseline variants validated and pinned
Canary automation: policy implemented in router and tested
Conformance tests: passed in CI for embeddings and rerank
Dashboards: latency, errors, quality, and fallback panels live in Console
Runbook: step-by-step rollback and manual fallback procedures documented and exercised
Docs: API reference, migration guide, SDK snippets published
Legal/Security: security review completed and KMS integration tested
Support: on-call rotation and run escalation path configured for first 30 days
dependencies: ENG-7010: rerank-kernel-optimizations (latency improvements for batched scoring)
PM-412087: hosted-surface-prd-degraded-rollout (relevant operational playbook that will be referenced)
SEC-210: kms-enterprise-integration (security sign-off and test keys)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regression on unseen customer prompt distributions. Mitigation: broaden eval corpus, run shadow traffic for 7 days before customer canary
Risk: Tail latency spikes under realistic multi-tenant load. Mitigation: synthetic stress tests, autoscaling knobs and per-tenant throttles configured
Risk: Fallback causes large quality drop and customer complaints. Mitigation: staged fallback to a slightly lower-capacity model with documented delta and opt-in beta customers for early feedback
Risk: Billing surprises due to rerank compute. Mitigation: publish cost estimates and add quotas/alerts for customers during canary
